## Grading philosophy
Simulation grades reflect the quality of analysis and decision-making.

::: {.callout-note}
You are **not** graded on whether your country "wins." You are graded on whether your decisions are economically defensible and well-justified.
:::

## Rubric (summary)
| Criterion | What we look for |
|---|---|
| Economic reasoning | Correct use of course concepts; clear causal logic |
| Policy coherence | Internally consistent package; realistic commitments |
| Use of evidence/theory | Connects choices to chapter frameworks |
| Role engagement | Recommendations match role objectives and constraints |
| Clarity and professionalism | Concise writing; clear recommendation |

::: {.callout-tip}
**How to improve quickly:** Start your memo with a specific recommendation, then justify it using 2–3 chapter concepts.
:::

## What earns a top score
- a coherent policy package that matches your regime and constraints
- explicit trade-offs (what you give up to achieve your goal)
- clear recognition of spillovers and political constraints
- consistent signaling over time, with justified adjustments

## Common pitfalls
- proposing mutually inconsistent policies (e.g., fixed peg + money creation + no reserves)
- shifting objectives week-to-week with no explanation
- vague memos that do not commit to a policy
- failing to submit a required document
